# Generated by iptables-save v1.8.10 on Wed Aug 27 09:00:00 2026
# A legacy FTP server behind a deny-postured firewall. The admin enabled the
# ftp conntrack helper so passive-mode data connections "just work" - but the
# helper opens RELATED pinholes from whatever it reads on the control channel,
# and the INPUT chain accepts RELATED like every stateful ruleset does. That
# is the whole hole: the helper, not a rule, decides which ports open.
*raw
:PREROUTING ACCEPT [0:0]
:OUTPUT ACCEPT [0:0]
-A PREROUTING -p tcp --dport 21 -j CT --helper ftp
COMMIT
*filter
:INPUT DROP [0:0]
:FORWARD DROP [0:0]
:OUTPUT ACCEPT [0:0]
-A INPUT -i lo -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate INVALID -j DROP
-A INPUT -p tcp --dport 21 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -p tcp --dport 22 -s 10.0.0.0/8 -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -m limit --limit 5/min -j LOG --log-prefix "input-drop: "
COMMIT
